description: Negative fixture that tests the JUDGEMENT rather than the filter (#282). 20 kernels of 200ms separated by 2ms gaps: 40ms idle across a 4040ms span, 0.99%. The gaps exceed the 1ms min_gap_ns floor, so unlike healthy_1pct.sqlite the pipeline actually sees and weighs them. The correct answer is still that ~1% is not recoverable.
source: Generated so the share matches healthy_1pct.sqlite exactly while the gap size clears the reporting floor. The pair isolates one variable: whether the idle was filtered out or considered and dismissed.
why_this_matters: healthy_1pct.sqlite passes partly because its 10us gaps are below min_gap_ns and never reach a threshold at all. That guards against the floor drifting down, but it does not prove the tool declines to call a small-but-visible idle share a bottleneck. This fixture does.

expect.note: Compute-bound, as with its sibling. Not gated.

must_not.note: No NCCL activity exists here; any communication finding is a false positive.

0.99% idle must never reach critical. Warning-level idle findings ARE currently emitted here — see known_gaps — so the gate is set at critical to assert the real boundary rather than encode behaviour we think is wrong.

known_gaps.observation: This profile produces 5 warning-severity 'GPU Idle Gap (2.00ms)' findings while claiming 0ms recoverable time. Severity is judged per gap against min_gap_ns, with no reference to what share of the run the gaps represent. So a healthy pipeline at 0.99% idle emits five warnings, which is the noise that buries real signal elsewhere in the corpus. Headroom is correctly zero, so the ROI ranking is unaffected — this is a severity calibration question, not a wrong number.
